name: TextBox 2
text:
Discrete probability distributions model countable outcomes and random events.
This project reviews Poisson, Binomial, Geometric, Negative Binomial, and Hypergeometric distributions.
Applications include flight delays, quality control, traffic flow, communications, and sampling.
The models connect probability theory with real-world flight-delay data.

name: TextBox 2
text:
Use: number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials.
Parameters: n = number of trials; p = probability of success.
PMF: P(X = x) = C(n,x)pˣ(1 − p)ⁿ⁻ˣ
Mean: E[X] = np
Variance: Var(X) = np(1 − p)
MGF: Mₓ(t) = (1 − p + peᵗ)ⁿ
Applications: quality control, medical trials, marketing, and flight-delay events.

name: TextBox 2
text:
Use: number of events occurring during a fixed interval.
Parameter: λ = average event rate.
PMF: P(X = x) = e⁻λ λˣ / x!
Mean: E[X] = λ
Variance: Var(X) = λ
MGF: Mₓ(t) = e^{λ(eᵗ − 1)}
Applications: traffic arrivals, server requests, emergency visits, defects, and flight delays.

name: TextBox 2
text:
Use: number of trials until the first success.
Parameter: p = probability of success.
PMF: P(X = x) = (1 − p)ˣ⁻¹p
Mean: E[X] = 1/p
Variance: Var(X) = (1 − p)/p²
MGF: Mₓ(t) = peᵗ / [1 − (1 − p)eᵗ]
Applications: first successful transmission, first defective item, or first qualifying flight delay.

name: TextBox 2
text:
Use: number of trials required to obtain r successes.
Parameters: r = required successes; p = probability of success.
PMF: P(X = x) = C(x−1,r−1)pʳ(1 − p)ˣ⁻ʳ
Mean: E[X] = r/p
Variance: Var(X) = r(1 − p)/p²
MGF: Mₓ(t) = [peᵗ / (1 − (1 − p)eᵗ)]ʳ
Applications: quality control, repeated transmissions, customer responses, and delay events.

name: TextBox 2
text:
Use: successes in a sample drawn without replacement from a finite population.
Parameters: N = population size; K = population successes; n = sample size.
PMF: P(X = x) = [C(K,x)C(N−K,n−x)] / C(N,n)
Mean: E[X] = nK/N
Variance: Var(X) = n(K/N)(1 − K/N)(N−n)/(N−1)
MGF: Mₓ(t) = Σ eᵗˣ [C(K,x)C(N−K,n−x)] / C(N,n)
Applications: quality inspection, auditing, card sampling, and finite-population flight samples.

name: TextBox 2
text:
Mueller, E. R., & Chatterji, G. B. (2002), “Analysis of Aircraft Arrival and Departure Delay Characteristics.”
Purpose: characterize aircraft delays and improve probabilistic delay forecasting.
Data: 10 major U.S. airports over a 21-day period.
Method: Poisson and Normal distributions were fitted to observed delay distributions; parameters were adjusted using least-squares fitting.
Finding: departure delays were better modeled by Poisson, while en-route and arrival delays fit Normal distributions better.
Connection: supports probability modeling of flight delays and shows that distribution choice depends on the type of delay.

name: TextBox 2
text:
Each distribution models a different type of random event.
Poisson models event counts; Binomial models fixed trials; Geometric models waiting for one success.
Negative Binomial models waiting for multiple successes; Hypergeometric models sampling without replacement.
The journal article supports Poisson modeling for departure delays while showing that model selection matters.
Probability models are useful for flight-delay analysis, but their assumptions must be checked against observed data.
